einzeiler: A deep dive into an episode featuring Joe's departure for Alert and a look at IBLP…
kurzfassung: The hosts recap a 2013 episode where the family sends Joseph off to nine weeks of boot camp at the Alert Academy. John David flies Joe to Texas while the rest of the family holds a going-away party and trainer Steve inspects the pantry. In the second half, the hosts review issues of the IBLP children's magazine Bright Arrows and discuss its manufactured testimonial stories.
stichpunkte: Michelle gives Joseph a buzz cut before he leaves for the Alert Academy in Texas.
John David flies his brother to Texas as he works toward getting his pilot's license.
Trainer Steve conducts a surprise pantry inspection that yields disappointing results.
Josh and Jim Bob complete a weigh-in and a workout session with Steve.
The hosts review IBLP's children's magazine, Bright Arrows, noting its dry and dull content.
An analysis of Bright Arrows reveals how testimonial stories were altered to remove negative outcomes.
The hosts discuss their childhood nostalgia for print magazines and collage projects.

clips.text: Joe makes a bizarre statement about wanting a shorter haircut since the moment he was born.
The hosts mock the absurdity of doing a weight-in check at the end of the day after eating a heavy meal.
Reading from an old magazine, the hosts mock the absurd hypothetical baby names suggested in an IBLP publication.
A cult magazine passage explains that a husband's duties include providing, protecting, instructing, and correcting his wife.
The hosts reflect on how confirmation finally proves that the emotional stories published in religious magazines were entirely fabricated.

beschreibung:
This episode has been rated TMJ, Too Much Joe. He spends quality time with Cannon followed by way too many people talking about how he’s an accountability partner and makesthe right decisions. Yeesh! Trainer Steve returns to make the mens suffer even more in their weight loss competition.

In the Dig, Whitney explores the short lived IBLP children’s magazine, Bright Arrows. We all know “Highlights” is the pinnacle of child-focused magazines, but this one isn’t even close. It fails to hit the mark.
